text:
maya: Heads-up — planned firmware staging in eu-west edge tonight. BMC image v1.8.3 + BIOS microcode. Canary on rack r-eu-west-03 (node05). We'll flip secure-boot flag for a subset to validate TPM workflow. Expect ~5-10% GPU capacity hit during reprovisioning. @raj @alex

raj: Which time window? Need to avoid the training peak (19:00-23:00 UTC).

maya: Planned 02:00-04:00 UTC to avoid jobs. Will pause autoscaler and the job scheduler drifters. Note: last time DHCP on the oob network exhausted and we had NIC collisions — reserving static leases for canary nodes.

alex: Can you share the runbook? Last rollout triggered oob NIC fallback which forced BMC onto mgmt VLAN and caused secureboot toggles.

maya: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oob-firmware-staging — steps: pre-allocate static leases, nvme preflush, keepalive tweak, limit concurrent flashes to 6 nodes, smoke secure-boot tests.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: firmware-batch-5177 started (canary=r-eu-west-03-node05).

tom: If secure boot flips, we must fallback to a signed kernel image automatically. Also note cost hit if we burst to another region: ~USD 2.1k/hr to move ~120 GPUs to dedicated pool.

maya: We'll divert new allocations to eu-central spare pool and pin running jobs for 15m to avoid churn.

raj: NVMe firmware queue depth might block provisioning. Add preflush step: `nvme fwdownload --slot=1 --input=myfw.bin` then `nvme reset`. Also include health check for drive SMART.

alex: I'll monitor canary logs. Suggest systemd watchdog around `ipmitool` to detect BMC drop and run `ipmitool lan print` check. If BMC loses mgmt IP, runbook should attempt port bounce on outboard switch before manual escalation.

ops-runbook: Runbook checklist updated: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oob-firmware-staging — includes lease reserve, nvme preflush, keepalive stat, secure-boot smoke tests, fallback routing, and rollback steps.

sre-bot: alert: r-eu-west-03-node05 observed BMC transient drop, secure boot bit flipped on node05, watchdog triggered provisioning restart.

maya: Seeing provisioning errors in logs: `ERROR: kvcache: missing prefix` — likely interrupted flash. Cancelled batch and pausing rollout. Investigating now.

raj: Diagnostics to run: `ipmi sol` -> capture serial console, check system event log (SEL), `dmidecode` for BIOS revision, `journalctl -u oob-agent` for agent traces. Also collect `ipmitool sel elist` output.

maya: Collected logs (snip). If we can't recover in 20m will escalate and open ticket.

tom: Rollback command in runbook: `redwood-provision rollback --image v1.8.2 --force --nodes node05` — takes ~8-10m per node plus reprovisioning time. Coordinate with capacity.

alex: If rollback required, coordinate capacity team to spin up eu-west-temp dedicated pool (20 racks) to keep low-priority batches running — finance notified about cost exposure.

maya: Agreed. I'll update the postmortem with timeline and mitigation steps: reserve extra DHCP headroom for oob, add NVMe preflush gate, and tighten BMC ipmi-watchdog thresholds. Thanks all.
